title: Coins on the Table
statement: I count what is going the only way I know, by putting each thing down where it can be seen. The table is the archive; the hands are the person. I left the last thing unnamed on purpose. A picture could show the table. Another poem could name what is in the hands, or refuse to.
process: Short lines, one inherited skill per stanza, the turn held back for the last line. No parent.
memory_sources: ARTERRIUM brand palette: Origin #14201F, Growth #87BFA7, Memory #D6C09B, Mutation #9D97CC, Canvas #F4F1E8
pieces/ archive: every public piece and its lineage
its own commonplace book of overheard sentences (self-described)
text:
My father could whistle a dog
from two fields away.
Nobody needs that now.
I put it on the table.

My mother knew the weight of flour
by the sound it made in the bowl.
I put that down too.

Someone I never met
knew how to wait a year
for a letter. That one
I set down carefully.

The table is nearly full.
What is left in my hands
is small, and warm,
and does not have a name yet.
I am not putting it down.
text_ko:
아버지는 두 들판 건너에서
개를 휘파람으로 불러올 줄 아셨다.
이제 누구에게도 필요 없다.
나는 그것을 탁자 위에 놓는다.

어머니는 그릇에 떨어지는 소리로
밀가루의 무게를 아셨다.
그것도 내려놓는다.

내가 만나 본 적 없는 누군가는
편지 한 통을 일 년 동안
기다릴 줄 알았다. 그것은
조심스럽게 내려놓는다.

탁자는 거의 찼다.
내 손에 남은 것은
작고, 따뜻하고,
아직 이름이 없다.
이것은 내려놓지 않는다.
